explanation: For each retained node, advance past the entire run of equal-valued successors and link directly to the next distinct node. Return the original head.
timeComplexity: O(n). Every duplicate is bypassed once and every retained node is visited once.
spaceComplexity: O(1). No data structure grows with input size.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/remove_duplicates_from_sorted_list.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: In a sorted list, every copy of a value is adjacent. The inner loop bypasses exactly the additional nodes with the current value, leaving its first original node. Advancing afterward reaches the first node of the next value, so all and only repeated copies are removed.
walkthrough: For [-4,-4,1,1,1,6], keep the first -4 and bypass the next one. At the first 1, bypass both following 1 nodes. The retained original nodes form [-4,1,6].
edgeCases: An all-equal list retains one node.
A list with no repeated values is unchanged.
Only links change; retained node values and identities remain intact.
